comparison: Perfect agreement on experimental design (C27-C29). Both evaluations find the design theoretically sound and appropriately controlled. OpenEval emphasizes the design controls for confounds; peer review praises how it equalizes evidence across correlations.

Both address trial-by-trial correlation computation (C54, C55, C57). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on statistical evidence, while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting the paradigm 'did not allow them to determine the origin of this bias' and calling the heuristics explanation speculative.

Perfect agreement on learning effects (C58-C61). Both evaluations support the findings showing dissociation between parameter changes and stable correlation estimates, with no concerns raised about the analyses.

Perfect agreement on comparison to prior literature (C77-C82). Both evaluations support the discussion of differences from economics literature and find the contextualization appropriate, though specific mechanisms remain speculative.

Both address neural mechanisms and broader context (C83-C85). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative neural claims requiring additional data; peer review rates as SUPPORTED, praising connections to prior work while acknowledging speculative nature of C85.

Both address theoretical derivation (C23-C25) with high overlap. OpenEval focuses on mathematical soundness; peer review emphasizes the 'elegant computational approach' and normative principles. Both find the theoretical foundation convincing. Peer review also includes C3 and C18.

Both address implications for evidence accumulation (C72-C74). OpenEval supports the inference about correlation-dependent adjustments; peer review supports the DDM framework insights. Peer review also includes C75-C76 on collapsing bounds.

Both address behavioral choice results (C30, C32, C33, C37). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor across individual and aggregate data; peer review confirms no impact on choice accuracy and notes this is consistent with correlation misestimation not affecting choices.

Overlapping coverage of behavioral results. OpenEval R3 addresses choice accuracy (C30-C37); peer R4 addresses RT effects (C31, C34-C36, C38). Both support their respective findings, with peer review noting effects 'largely restricted to response times.'

Both address RT patterns and theoretical predictions (C38). OpenEval notes qualitative match with simulations; peer review confirms RT impacts suggesting deviation from normative strategy. Both support the findings.

Both address simulation-based inferences (C41-C44). OpenEval supports qualitative match between data and simulations; peer review explicitly discusses how simulations show correlation misestimation affects only RT, not choices.
Both address parameter variability (C52). OpenEval supports the finding with speculative interpretation; peer review supports without challenge, consistent with overall pattern reviewers endorse.

Both address model comparison and main conclusions (C46 overlap). OpenEval emphasizes formal model comparison methods; peer review focuses on broader conclusion about near-normative behavior with correlation underestimation. Both support findings.

Both address modeling results (C48 overlap). OpenEval supports model comparison showing full-ρ^ model best; peer review praises modeling approach showing 'impressively deep understanding' of DDM parameter relationships.

Both address parameter relationships (C50 overlap). OpenEval supports correlation analysis with significance testing; peer review describes 'intriguing result' of correlation underestimation pattern from modeling.

Both address model parameters (C49 overlap). OpenEval supports statistical analysis of fit parameters; peer review praises modeling approach demonstrating rational evidence weighting under correlation misestimation assumption.

Both address parameter variability and performance (C53 overlap). OpenEval supports quantitative analysis with speculative explanation; peer review supports modeling framework showing relationships between DDM parameters.

Both address main findings summary (C62, C87 overlap). OpenEval supports conclusions based on convergent evidence; peer review affirms 'convincing' demonstration and praises limited training making behavior 'natural.'

Both address main findings (C3 overlap). OpenEval supports abstract-level summary claims; peer review affirms theoretical contribution showing how humans make decisions about correlated observations.

Both address main findings summary (C4, C5 overlap). OpenEval supports abstract claims as accurate representation; peer review describes 'intriguing result' about correlation underestimation and praises convincing demonstration.
